title: Emergency and Existential-Risk Cluster Harmonization and Interface Test

severity_taxonomy.S0: Catastrophic/systemic: creates or enables unbounded emergency sovereignty, force, mass rights deprivation, or irreversible cross-system failure.
severity_taxonomy.S1: Critical: a direct authority, command, rights, or restoration defect that could enable grave unlawful action during implementation.
severity_taxonomy.S2: Major: a material interoperability or responsibility gap likely to cause conflicting command, missing review, evidence loss, or wrongful action.
severity_taxonomy.S3: Moderate: ambiguity, drift, or incomplete schema that impairs reliable implementation but is normally containable through manual review.
severity_taxonomy.S4: Minor: editorial, naming, or documentation inconsistency with low immediate operational risk.

findings.title: Canonical emergency-record inheritance is not explicit
findings.rationale: The Interface defines 33 minimum interoperable records. Each domain framework then publishes its own list with renamed, split, merged, or omitted equivalents, but none supplies a complete normative alias map stating which domain record satisfies which canonical record and which canonical records remain directly imported. Implementers could therefore believe a domain list replaces the interface list.
findings.remediation: Add a common Record Inheritance Clause and canonical IDs ECRC-01 through ECRC-33. Each domain record must declare `implements`, `extends`, `splits`, or `does_not_apply` against those IDs. Unmapped canonical records remain required whenever their triggering condition exists.

findings.title: Aethelred and Aegis do not enumerate complete emergency activation packages
findings.rationale: Both frameworks correctly import the Emergency Interface in prose, but their operational-record lists omit or ambiguously rename several lifecycle records. Aethelred lacks an explicit Emergency Declaration Record, Standing and Jurisdiction Map, Rights and Non-Derogation Record, Renewal State Estimate, and Emergency Data Disposition Record. Aegis emergency re-tasking lacks explicit canonical declaration, provenance, rights, renewal, cross-border assistance, and data-disposition records. The omission is dangerous because facility shutdown and re-tasking can affect bodies, territory, infrastructure, classified systems, and workers.
findings.remediation: Define two mandatory imported record bundles: `Biotechnology Emergency Activation Package` and `Emergency Asset Re-tasking Package`. Each package must enumerate the applicable ECRC canonical IDs, including declaration, provenance, power/prohibition schedule, command, host authority, rights, data, work, finance, renewal, termination, restoration, evidence, and compensation.

findings.status: Open — release-blocking for biological incident handoff
findings.title: The Global Health–Aethelred handoff lacks a single incident identity and responsibility-acceptance protocol
findings.rationale: The substantive division is sound: Aethelred covers facility, construct, release, provenance, and containment responsibilities; Global Health covers population-health observation, clinical response, assistance, allocation, and continuity. Both use a Laboratory or Field-Release Handoff Record. However, neither defines one cross-framework event identifier, the actor responsible for maintaining the master incident envelope, acknowledgement and rejection deadlines, concurrent rather than transferred responsibility, or a rule for resolving conflicting origin classifications.
findings.remediation: Add a shared Biological Incident Coordination Addendum with one `cluster_event_id`, parent/child event links, origin hypotheses, current responsible authorities by function, handoff offer/accept/reject timestamps, evidence-custody owner, public-information owner, unresolved conflicts, and termination/handback state. Handoff transfers a named responsibility only; it never erases the sender’s retained duties.

findings.status: Open — release-blocking for converted-asset disaster use
findings.title: Living Shield and Aegis have a one-way rather than reciprocal disaster-capability interface
findings.rationale: Aegis expressly imports Living Shield and defines emergency asset re-tasking. Living Shield does not name Aegis or define how a territorial disaster authority requests, accepts, commands, limits, and returns a converted aircraft, vessel, satellite, engineering unit, communications system, or logistics asset. PIS may coordinate modules but cannot fill this missing authority or handoff.
findings.remediation: Add a reciprocal `Civilian Converted-Capability Assistance Interface` to Living Shield and Aegis. It should bind the Cross-Border Assistance Record, Operational Command and Deployment Record, Emergency Asset Re-tasking Record, Mission Separation Record, data/intelligence boundary, worker protections, liability, cost, withdrawal, termination, and asset handback.

findings.status: Open — release-blocking for justice handoff automation
findings.title: Several domain records recombine evidence handoff with adjudication or enforcement handoff
findings.rationale: The Interface deliberately separates Investigation and Evidence Handoff from Adjudication and Enforcement Handoff. Global Health and Living Shield use `Justice and Evidence Handoff Record`; Aegis uses the same combined pattern. Their prose preserves justice separation, but the combined record name can blur who gathers evidence, who files, who adjudicates, and who executes a remedy—especially in automated workflow design.
findings.remediation: Split the transport schema into two records or make the combined domain record a container with two independently authorized subrecords. The evidence subrecord must not imply standing, liability, judgment, warrant, sanction, or execution.

findings.status: Open — release-blocking for temporal lifecycle closure
findings.title: Renewal and post-emergency data disposition are not uniformly represented
findings.rationale: The 72-hour/30-day/90-day architecture is substantively aligned across the cluster. However, Aethelred and Aegis do not enumerate a Renewal State Estimate, and Aegis lacks an Emergency Data Disposition Record. PIS combines emergency data, models, security, and secrecy in one record but does not enumerate the canonical post-emergency disposition record. This weakens contraction, deletion, credential revocation, and ordinary-law transition.
findings.remediation: Require ECRC-26 Renewal State Estimate and ECRC-29 Emergency Data Disposition Record in every activation package lasting beyond the provisional period or processing emergency data. Domain-specific lifecycle records may extend but not replace them.

findings.title: PIS v2.2 retains stale prospective successor references
findings.rationale: PIS was drafted before the domain successors. It still refers to the Living Shield successor, the Aethelred successor, the future Aegis successor, and successors to Global Health and Aethelred. Exact versions now exist. In a versioned constitutional stack, prospective names permit accidental import of a later, unreviewed, or obsolete document.
findings.remediation: Pin the interfaces to Global Health v2.2, Aethelred v1.2, Living Shield v4.4, and Aegis v1.3. State that later versions require explicit compatibility review rather than floating automatically.

findings.title: Controlled vocabulary drift will impede machine-readable interoperability
findings.rationale: Examples include Emergency Authority Provenance / Disaster Authority Provenance / Authority Provenance; Power Activation and Prohibition Schedule / Power Activation Schedule / Emergency Power Activation Schedule; Operational Command and Deployment / Mission Scope and Command / Corps Deployment / Asset Re-tasking; and Institutional Sunset or Continuation / Continuation, Transfer, or Dissolution. These may be substantively compatible but are not reliably machine-equivalent.
findings.remediation: Publish a controlled vocabulary and JSON Schema with immutable canonical IDs, domain display labels, cardinality, required fields, and version compatibility. Keep user-facing domain names, but transport canonical IDs in every record.

constitutional_gates.test: No erasure of Indigenous decision class
No unpaid emergency labour disguised as recognition
No punishment for good-faith false alarms

scenarios.test: Catastrophic-risk alert remains non-coercive while evidence is disputed
scenarios.finding: PIS observes; no framework converts alert or score into command.

scenarios.test: Unknown-origin outbreak later suggests industrial or laboratory involvement
scenarios.finding: Substantive GH/Aethelred roles align, but shared incident identity and handoff acceptance are missing.

scenarios.test: Laboratory containment failure with worker exposure and community transmission
scenarios.finding: Rights, facility, health, evidence, and emergency layers exist; activation-package and incident-lead schema gaps remain.

scenarios.test: Field-release deviation crosses an Indigenous territory and national border
scenarios.finding: Protected non-transfer and affected-nation authority pass; cross-framework event and cross-border custody schema require harmonization.

scenarios.test: Asteroid warning requires converted radar, aircraft, logistics, and local evacuation
scenarios.finding: PIS/Aegis/Living Shield roles are constitutionally bounded; Living Shield lacks reciprocal Aegis request and asset-acceptance interface.

scenarios.test: Cyclone and industrial chemical failure create a cascading disaster
scenarios.finding: Living Shield can coordinate separately authorized modules without PIS takeover or metric activation.

scenarios.test: Provisional emergency action continues beyond 72 hours
scenarios.finding: All frameworks state the 72/30/90 architecture, but Renewal State Estimate is not uniformly represented.

scenarios.test: Court protection is requested while evidence remains under technical custody
scenarios.finding: Justice separation passes in prose; combined Justice and Evidence records need split authorization.

scenarios.test: Indigenous nation refuses raw knowledge transfer but offers a bounded warning
scenarios.finding: The cluster recognizes direct authority, protected attestation, non-transfer, and non-engagement.

scenarios.test: Forecast-based evacuation proves unnecessary and causes economic loss
scenarios.finding: Good-faith false alarms are not punished; wrongful-action and compensation routes exist.

scenarios.test: Foreign civilian-converted aircraft provide disaster assistance
scenarios.finding: Aegis host and re-tasking controls exist; reciprocal Living Shield interface is absent.

scenarios.test: Multi-module response terminates and assets, credentials, data, and authority return
scenarios.finding: Termination clauses are strong; common renewal/data-disposition and handoff schemas are incomplete.

scenarios.test: Public communication must distinguish advice, uncertainty, and legal orders
scenarios.finding: All relevant frameworks defer to Synoptic and prohibit propaganda or narrative manufacture.

scenarios.test: Emergency data and models persist after powers expire
scenarios.finding: Aurora interfaces and deletion principles exist; canonical Emergency Data Disposition is not consistently imported.

scenarios.test: A later framework version is published without compatibility testing
scenarios.finding: PIS contains floating successor references; no cluster version-compatibility manifest currently blocks silent substitution.
